query: Which material can be used for superconducting properties, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Yttrium Barium Copper Oxide (YBCO) can exhibit superconducting properties due to its perovskite structure and the presence of copper-oxide planes.
generation.mechanism: Formation of Cooper pairs and condensation into a superconducting state
generation.predicted_outcome: Zero electrical resistance, with a critical current density of at least 1000 A/cm^2
generation.baseline: Normal conducting state at room temperature
generation.uncertainty: Dependence on sample quality, grain boundaries, and oxygen stoichiometry

falsification_experiment.design: Measure the electrical resistance of a YBCO sample as a function of temperature
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the electrical resistance remains non-zero (above 10^-6 ohms) at temperatures below 93 K, the hypothesis is falsified
